transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because for the past few weeks, I've just felt this... this heavy, sad pressure sitting on me pretty much all day. Even when I'm at work and I'm putting on a smile for my patients, inside I just feel like I'm barely holding myself together right now.
Have you ever had a period—lasting several days or more—where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual, even if it wasn't during this current low mood?

No, I don't think so. Um... I've never really had a time where I felt unusually energetic or elated like that. I definitely always need my sleep, especially with my shifts. So, no, I haven't experienced anything like what you're describing.
How long have you been experiencing this persistent sad, heavy feeling—has it been going on for a few weeks, or longer, like months or years?
It's been going on for about three weeks now. Um, it started pretty shortly after I found out I was pregnant.
Over these past three weeks, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you'd normally enjoy, even when you're not at work?

Yeah, I have. Usually, after my shifts, I have things I do to decompress... I used to paint, or I'd go to yoga, or even salsa dancing. But lately, I just don't have it in me. I just go straight home, sit on the couch, and... I even ignore my texts. It just feels like none of it is really worth the effort right now.
Have you been having any thoughts of worthlessness, excessive guilt, or thoughts of harming yourself during these past three weeks?

No, I haven't had any thoughts of harming myself. I don't have a plan or anything like that. But... what really scared me, and why I actually said something at my prenatal appointment, is that I have been having these thoughts where I just wish I wouldn't wake up. It's just this feeling of not wanting to be here, even though I wouldn't actually do anything to hurt myself. And yeah, I guess I have been feeling pretty worthless, too. Like I'm just not doing a good job at anything right now.

Over these past three weeks, how much has this affected your ability to keep up with your work shifts and daily responsibilities—are you still managing to get through them, even if it's hard, or have you found yourself unable to function at all on some days?

I'm still making it to work, yeah. I haven't called out or anything. But... it's definitely getting harder to keep up, and it's starting to show. My supervisor actually brought it up recently—she noticed some incomplete charting on my end, which really isn't like me. 

And then outside of work, like I mentioned, I've just been pulling away from my friends and all the normal things that usually keep me steady. So I'm still getting through the days, I guess, but just doing the bare minimum.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep over these past three weeks—such as trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?

No, I haven't really noticed any changes there. My sleep has been pretty normal, actually. I don't have any trouble falling asleep or staying asleep, and I'm not sleeping way more than usual either. That part of my routine is still okay.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight over these past three weeks, such as eating significantly more or less than usual?

Yeah, my appetite has definitely changed. I know I should be eating regularly, especially with being pregnant and all, but most days... food just sounds completely unappealing. Like, I'll be halfway through my clinic shift and suddenly realize all I've had all day is just some crackers or a cup of coffee. I'm just not eating as much as I normally would.
Have you noticed any difficulty concentrating, focusing, or making decisions—at work or in daily life—over these past three weeks?

Yeah, I definitely have. My brain just feels really foggy lately. Like at work, I keep finding myself rereading medication orders and wound-care notes over and over because it's just not sticking. And then with decisions... things I normally just do automatically, I find myself freezing up. I just end up second-guessing myself on almost everything right now.
Have you or others noticed you moving, speaking, or reacting more slowly than usual, or conversely feeling unusually restless and unable to sit still?

Yeah, I've definitely noticed the slowing down part. I'm not restless at all, but everything I do just feels... really slowed down. It's honestly like I'm moving through syrup. Even just simple things at the clinic, you know, like gathering wound supplies for a patient or trying to finish my charting... it all just takes me noticeably longer than it should right now.

Outside of work, how are you managing basic day-to-day things like taking care of yourself—showering, eating regularly, or keeping up with household tasks—are you still able to do these, or has it become really difficult to manage even those?

It's become really difficult, honestly. I mean, I’m still making it to work, but even there, my supervisor has already noticed my incomplete charting. And outside of work... I've just been pulling away from my friends and the things that usually keep me steady. I just don't have the energy to keep up with much else right now.
Have you noticed a marked decrease in your energy level or increased fatigue over these past three weeks, even after getting adequate rest?

Honestly, I'm not really sure if it's worse than usual. I mean, I'm tired, but I haven't really noticed a huge drop in my energy or anything like that. I just feel kind of drained, but I don't think it's anything extreme.
